s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute progressive parkinsonian syndrome with bilateral upper limb rigidity and gait disturbance
key_facts: 64-year-old woman
5-year history of diabetes mellitus
On maintenance dialysis for 2 years
History of hypertension and breast cancer
Episode of vomiting and diarrhea 1 month prior to presentation
Gradual development of difficulty in moving extremities
Low-volume voice and slow speech
Difficulty in getting up or walking steadily
Blood pressure: 163/76 mmHg
Normal blood tests
Normal vitamin B1, thyroid function, and lactate levels
Normal blood gas analysis without acidosis
Normal spinal fluid test
Brain MRI showed high-intensity areas in bilateral lenticular nucleus with lentiform fork sign

shortlist.label: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute progressive parkinsonian syndrome with bilateral upper limb rigidity and gait disturbance, consistent with PSP

shortlist.label: Multiple System Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Parkinsonian features, autonomic dysfunction, and cerebellar ataxia, which can be seen in MSA

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Asymmetric parkinsonism, rigidity, and dystonia, consistent with CBD

shortlist.label: Parkinson's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Classic parkinsonian symptoms, including bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremor

shortlist.label: Vascular Parkinsonism
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension and diabetes, which are risk factors for vascular parkinsonism

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including difficulty in moving extremities, low-volume voice, slow speech, mask-like face, hypophonia, bradykinesia, rigidity, and gait disturbance, are consistent with Parkinson's Disease. The brain MRI showing high-intensity areas in bilateral lenticular nucleus with lentiform fork sign also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
rejected.why: Lack of prominent supranuclear vertical gaze palsy

rejected.label: Multiple System Atrophy
rejected.why: No clear evidence of autonomic dysfunction or cerebellar ataxia

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: No asymmetric motor symptoms or alien limb phenomenon

rejected.label: Vascular Parkinsonism
rejected.why: No clear evidence of vascular lesions on imaging studies
